extracted.subtask_description: Contemporary newspaper reporting of World War II battlefield, air and naval actions, synthesizing official communiqués, correspondent dispatches, and wire-service reports into front-page news items. Emphasizes attribution, geographic detail, operational context, and cautious language where verification is incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute claims and facts to specific sources (e.g., 'Allied communique said', 'German radio admitted', 'the Italians said', 'the Admiralty announced', 'Reuters reported', 'Associated Press war correspondent').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the origin of each factual claim; use named official communiqués, national radio broadcasts, correspondents, or wire services rather than presenting unattributed assertions as fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of cautious/qualifying language when verification is incomplete
rubrics_metrics.description: Use qualifiers such as 'probable', 'reported', 'claimed', 'indicated', 'initial reports indicate', and note when 'clouds obscured the results.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid definitive statements about outcomes when evidence is obscured or conflicting; flag uncertainty and the reason (e.g., weather, lack of confirmation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Give precise locations and distances (e.g., 'El Guetar, seventy-three miles northwest of Gabes', 'twelve miles beyond Gafsa', 'the Mareth Line', 'Sened station, twenty-eight miles east of Gafsa').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide place names, directional bearings and mileages to situate readers and convey operational scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational/tactical context and strategic significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why an action matters tactically or strategically (e.g., 'entrance of Guetaria Pass, through which an attack might be made against Marshal Rommel’s flank', 'Should Patton reach the coast, the Nazi marshal would be cut off').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect battlefield gains or losses to broader campaign consequences to help readers understand implications beyond the immediate action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weather and environmental factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Report environmental conditions affecting operations (e.g., 'heavy rains and floods', 'muddy gullies of chilly water', 'clouds obscured the results', 'thin ice coating the river').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note how weather, terrain, or logistical conditions influenced tactics, movement, air operations and the ability to verify results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify outcomes with attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide counts and types of losses/damage (e.g., 'British submarines sank seven more supply ships', '14 German tanks destroyed', '19 buildings blasted', 'some 1,000 persons killed—Reuters reported', 'largest bag of the year' for aircraft destroyed) and attribute those numbers to sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give numeric detail where available but attribute figures to the reporting party and note discrepancies between sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present multiple perspectives including enemy statements and propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: Include opposing-side claims (e.g., German communiqués or radio admissions, Italian statements, Vichy broadcasts) alongside Allied accounts and note contradictions ('German radio admitted the loss of Gafsa—but declared “an Axis local offensive ... is progressing favorably”').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both sides' statements to provide balance, and mark when one side's claims conflict with others or with independent reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bylines and correspondent identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the reporter and wire-service credit when using front-line dispatches (e.g., 'By EDWARD KENNEDY, Associated Press War Correspondent').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include bylines for accountability and to signal first-hand reporting vs. aggregated wire copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use direct quotes for notable remarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Include direct quotations for human-interest or authoritative comments (e.g., LaGuardia: 'If I could fake my age, I'd join the army.'; 'the blow “particularly effective.”').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quoted material to convey voice, color, or official language while attributing speakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and cite direct evidence when available
rubrics_metrics.description: Note when physical evidence or reconnaissance confirms reports (e.g., 'The destruction was proved by photographs', 'headquarters said photographs showed damage').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite photographic, aerial reconnaissance or captured documents as higher-grade confirmation and explain what they show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare scale and historical significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Place actions in comparative/historical perspective (e.g., 'the largest American aerial armada yet sent against Germany', 'the deepest penetration into Germany proper').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signal when an operation marks a record or notable escalation to convey its importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report timing and nature of operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe when and how operations occurred (e.g., 'attacked Naples ... once during daylight and again after dark', 'by day and night', 'night fighters', 'daylight attacks on Germany proper').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give temporal details (day/night, dates) and operational mode (air raid, patrol, torpedo attack) to clarify the action's character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag contradictory casualty/damage reports and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight and contextualize wide variances in reported casualties/damage (e.g., Reuters' 'upwards of 1,000 persons killed in Berlin' vs Nazi admission of 48) and note when figures are 'not yet available' or 'not given.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make readers aware of conflicting tallies, their sources, and the likelihood of exaggeration or underreporting; avoid presenting any single disputed figure as definitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid, accessible leads and headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead with a concise summary and compelling headline (e.g., 'Americans Gain in Fattiela Mud. & Take Town 12 Miles Past Gafsas', 'U. S. Forces RECAPTURE EL GUETAR'), summarizing key who/what/where/when.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-load the most newsworthy facts to orient readers immediately; headlines should capture the principal development without overstating unverified details.
